en: In the miracle as an action, a connection of cause and effect is given to the understanding and the domain of its concepts is acknowledged; but at the same time its domain is thereby destroyed, in that the cause is not something as determinate as the effect, but is supposed to be something infinite; since the connection of cause and effect in the understanding is the sameness of determinateness, their opposition only this, that in the one this determinateness is activity, in the other passivity, — here, however, in the action itself an infinite, with infinite activity, is at the same time supposed to have a most limited effect.
Not the sublation of the domain of the understanding, but that it is at the same time posited and sublated, is what is unnatural.
Just as, on the one hand, the positing of an infinite cause contradicts the positing of a finite effect, so the infinite equally cancels the determinate effect.

There, viewed from the standpoint of the understanding, the infinite is only a negative, the indeterminate, to which something determinate is attached; here, from the side of the infinite as something that is, it is a spirit that acts, and the determinateness of the effect of a spirit is its negative side; only from another standpoint, in comparison, can its action appear determinate; in itself, according to its being, it is the sublation of a determinateness and in itself infinite.
zh: 在作为行动的奇迹里，知性被给予了一个原因和结果的关联，它的概念的领域也得到了承认；但同时它的领域又被这样摧毁：原因并不像结果那样是一个如此确定的东西，而应当是一个无限者；因为在知性里原因和结果的关联就是规定性的相同，它们的对立只在于，在其中一个里这种规定性是能动，在另一个里是受动，——而在这里，在行动本身里，一个具有无限能动的无限者却同时应当有一个极其有限的结果。
不自然的不是知性领域遭到扬弃，而是它同时被设定又被扬弃。
正如一方面设定一个无限的原因与设定一个有限的结果相矛盾，无限者也同样扬弃那确定的结果。
在那里，从知性的观点来看，无限者只是一个否定性的东西、那个不确定者，一个确定的东西被接在它上面；而在这里，从作为存在者的无限者这一方面来看，它是一个起作用的精神，一个精神的结果的规定性就是它否定的一面；只有从比较中的另一个观点出发，它的行动才能显得是确定的，而自在、就它的存在而言，它是对一种规定性的扬弃，并且在自身中是无限的。

en: When a god acts, it is only from spirit to spirit; the activity presupposes an object on which it is exercised; but the effect of the spirit is the sublation of that object.

The going-forth of the divine is only a development, that it, in sublating the opposite, presents itself in the union; but in the miracles the spirit appears as acting on bodies, [and then] the cause would not be a formed spirit whose form, considered merely in its opposition, could as body enter, equal to another and opposable to it, into the connection of cause and effect; this connection would be a community of the spirit, which is spirit only insofar as it has nothing in common with the body, and of the body, which is body because it has nothing in common with the spirit, but spirit and body have nothing in common; they are absolute opposites.

Their union, in which their opposition ceases, is a life, i.e. formed spirit; and when this acts as something divine, undivided, its doing is a marriage with kindred essence, with the divine, and a generation, a development of something new, of the presentation of their union; but insofar as the spirit acts in another, opposed form as something hostile, dominating, it has forgotten its divinity.
Miracles are therefore the presentation of the most ungodly, because they are the most unnatural and contain, bound together, the hardest opposition of spirit and body in all its monstrous crudeness.
Divine doing is the restoration and presentation of unity; miracle, the utmost tearing-apart.

The expectation that has been stirred up — to raise to divinity, through miraculous activities of this actual being, the actuality associated with the transfigured Jesus exalted to a god — is therefore so far from being fulfilled that it rather increases all the more the harshness of this addition of something actual.

Yet it is that much greater for us than for the members of the first Christian congregation, by as much more understanding as we have than they, who, breathed upon by the Oriental spirit, had completed the separation of spirit and body less fully and had delivered less to the understanding as objects.
Where we cognize determinate actuality, historical objectivity with the understanding, there is often spirit for them; and where we posit only pure spirit, there it is still embodied for them.

Of the latter kind of view, the form in which they grasp what we call immortality, namely the immortality of the soul, is an example; it appears to them as a resurrection of the body; both views are the extremes between which the Greek spirit [stands]; the one is the extreme of reason, which sets a soul, a negative as against all understanding, and its object, the dead body, over against each other, the other is the extreme of, so to speak, a positive capacity of reason, which posits the body as living while at the same time it assumed it to be dead; whereas for the Greeks body and soul remain in one living form, in the two extremes, by contrast, death is a separation of body and soul, and in the one the body is nothing more to the soul, in the other the body is something that persists even without life.

In other matters, where we cognize only with the understanding something actual or — which amounts to the same — some alien spirit, the first Christians mix in their own spirit; in the writings of the Jews we see past histories, individual situations and the former spirit of men, in the Jewish acts of worship a commanded doing whose spirit, purpose and thoughts no longer are for us and no longer have any truth; for them all this still had truth and spirit, but their truth, their spirit — they did not let it become objective.

The spirit which they give to passages of the prophets and of other Jewish books is, in their sense, neither — with regard to the prophets — the opinion of finding in them predictions of actualities, nor, on their side, the application to actuality.
It is an uncertain, formless hovering between actuality and spirit; on the one hand, in actuality only the spirit is considered, on the other hand actuality itself as such is present, but not fixed.

To give an example, John (12, 14 ff.) relates to the circumstance that Jesus rode into Jerusalem on a donkey an expression of the prophet, whose inspiration saw such a procession, [and] John lets it find its truth in the procession of Jesus.

The proofs that similar passages of the Jewish books are in part cited, in themselves, incorrectly against the literal sense of the original text, in part explained against their sense, which they receive through their context, in part refer to quite other actualities, to circumstances and men contemporary with the prophets, in part are merely isolated inspiration of the prophets, — all these proofs hit only the actuality of the relation which the apostles set up between them and the circumstances of Jesus' life, not their truth and spirit, just as little as their truth is visible in the strict objective assumption that the actual words and visions of the prophets were the earlier expression of later actualities.

The spirit of the relation which Christ's friends find between the visions of the prophets and the events of Jesus would be conceived too weakly if it were placed merely in the comparison of similarity of situations, in a comparison such as [that by which] we often add to the presentation of a situation the definite expression of old writers.

In the example cited above, John says expressly that Jesus' friends recognized these relations only after Jesus had been glorified, after the spirit had come upon them; had John seen in this relation a mere fancy, a mere similarity of different things, this remark would not have been needed; but as it is, in the spirit that vision of the prophet and this circumstance in an action of Jesus are one; and since the relation is only in the spirit, the objective view of it as a concurrence of actual things, of individual things, falls away.
This spirit, which fixes the actual just as little, or turns it into something indeterminate, and cognizes in it nothing individual but something spiritual, is especially also [to be found in] John

11, 51 visible, where John, in connection with the maxim of Caiaphas and its application, that it is better that one man die for the people than that the whole come into danger, reminds [us] that Caiaphas did not speak this for himself as an individual, but as high priest in prophetic inspiration (πϱοεϕήτευσεν).

What we would perhaps regard from the standpoint of an instrument of divine providence, in that John saw something filled by the spirit, since the character of the view of Jesus and his friends could not be more opposed to anything than to the standpoint of taking everything as machine, tool, instrument, but was rather the highest faith in spirit; and where one sees a unity of the concurrence of actions which, taken singly for themselves, lack this unity, the intention of the whole of the effect, and regards these actions (like those of Caiaphas) as subjected to it, ruled and guided by it without consciousness in their relation to the unity, as actualities and instruments, there John sees unity of the spirit and, in this action itself, the spirit of the whole effect acting; he speaks of Caiaphas as himself filled by the spirit in which the necessity of Jesus' fate lay.
zh: 当一个神起作用时，这只是从精神到精神；作用以一个它施加于其上的对象为前提；但精神的结果就是对这对象的扬弃。

神性者的走出只是一种发展，即它在扬弃对立者时把自身展示在结合里；但在奇迹里，精神显现为作用于身体，那样原因就不会是一个有形态的精神，因为这样一种精神的形态若只在它的对立中来看，作为身体本可以作为一个与另一个相等、并可与另一个相对立的东西进入原因和结果的关联；这种关联就会是精神与身体的一种共同体，而这个精神之所以是精神，只因为它与身体没有任何共同之处，这个身体之所以是身体，只因为它与精神没有任何共同之处，但精神和身体没有任何共同之处；它们是绝对对立的东西。
它们的结合——在结合中它们的对立停止了——是一种生命，即有形态的精神；当这个精神作为神性的、不可分离的东西起作用时，它的作为就是一种与同类本质、与神性者的婚配，并且是新的东西的产生和发展，是对它们的结合的展示；但就精神在另一种对立的形态中作为敌对的、统治性的东西起作用而言，它就忘记了自己的神性。
奇迹因此是最不神圣者的展示，因为它们是最不自然的，并且把精神和身体最坚硬的对立连同它全部骇人的粗野一并联结着包含在内。
神性的作为是统一的重建和展示；奇迹则是极端的撕裂。
因此，那个被激发起来的期待——即通过这个现实者的奇迹般的活动，把与那位得了荣耀、被提升为神的耶稣联系在一起的现实性提升到神性——非但没有得到满足，反倒更加增强了这种把一个现实者附加上的生硬。
不过，它对我们来说要比对最初基督教教团的成员来说大得多，正如我们的知性比他们的更多；他们受东方精神的吹拂，把精神和身体的分离完成得不够彻底，交给知性作为对象的东西也更少。
凡是我们用知性认识确定的现实性、历史客观性的地方，在他们那里往往就是精神；而凡是我们只设定纯粹精神的地方，这精神在他们那里还是具有身体的。

后一种观点的一个例子，就是他们用来把握我们称之为不死、而且是灵魂不死的那种东西的形式；它在他们那里显现为肉体的复活；这两种观点是希腊精神处于其间的两个极端；前一个是对立起灵魂——一个与一切知性相对立的否定性东西——及其对象即死去的身体的理性之极端，后一个可以说是理性的另一种肯定能力的极端，这种能力把身体设定为活的，同时却又把它当作死的；而对于希腊人来说，肉体和灵魂停留在一种活生生的形态里，在这两个极端里，死亡却是肉体和灵魂的分离，在一个极端里肉体对灵魂来说什么也不是了，在另一个极端里肉体即使没有生命也仍然留存。

在另一些事情上，我们只用知性去认识某种现实的东西，或者——这两者是一回事——去认识某种陌生的精神，这时最初的基督徒就把自己的精神掺和进去；在犹太人的书里我们看到的是一段段过去的历史、一个个个别的处境和人们曾经有过的精神，在犹太人的礼拜行动中看到的是被命令的行为，这种行为的精神、目的和思想对于我们来说已经不复存在，不再有任何真理；而对他们来说，这一切还曾具有真理和精神，但那是他们的真理、他们的精神，他们并没有让它成为客观的。
他们赋予先知书和其他犹太书中的段落的那种精神，在他们的意思里，既不是就先知而言要在其中找到关于现实性的预言的看法，也不是他们这边对现实性的应用。
这是一种在现实性和精神之间不确定的、无形态的飘浮；一方面，在现实性中只被考察到精神，另一方面，现实性本身作为这样的东西是现成的，却没有被固定下来。
举一个例子：约翰（12, 14 ff.）把先知的一句话联系到耶稣骑着一头驴进入耶路撒冷这件事上；那位先知的灵感曾看见这样一支队伍，约翰就让这句话在耶稣的这支队伍里找到它的真理。

这些证明——即犹太书中类似的段落，一部分自在地就是违背原文的字面意义被引用的，一部分是违背它们通过上下文获得的含义而被解释的，一部分涉及完全另一些现实性、涉及与先知同时代的情况和人，一部分只是先知孤立的灵感——所有这些证明只击中使徒在它们和耶稣的生活境况之间建立起来的那种关系的现实性，而没有击中它们的真理和精神；正如它们的真理也不可能在那种严格客观的假定中显现出来，即先知实际说过的话和实际看见的异象是后来的现实性的较早表达。
基督的朋友们在先知的异象和耶稣的事件之间发现的那种关系的精神，如果只被放在对种种处境相似性的比较里，被放在这样一种比较里——就像我们常常给对某个处境的描述附上古代作家的某个确定说法那样——那就被理解得太弱了。
在上面所举的例子中，约翰明确地说，耶稣的朋友们是在耶稣得了荣耀、在精神降临到他们身上之后，才认识到这些关系的；如果约翰在这种关系里看到的只是一种突然的念头、不同事物的一种单纯相似，那么这一说明本来就不需要；但情形既然如此，在精神里，先知的那个异象和耶稣某次行动中的这个情况就是一回事；而由于这种关系只在精神里，把它看作种种现实的东西、种种个别的东西的凑合的那种客观观点就消失了。
这种精神对现实的东西同样不予固定，或者把它变成一种不确定的东西，并且在其中认识到的不是任何个别的东西，而是一种精神性的东西，它尤其还见于约翰
11, 51 处可以看到：约翰在谈到该亚法的准则及其运用——即一个人为民众而死，总比整个民众陷入危险要好——时提醒说，该亚法说这话并不是以个人的身份为自己说的，而是作为大祭司在预言的灵感中说的（πϱοεϕήτευσεν）。

我们也许会从上帝护佑的一个工具这一观点去看的东西，约翰在其中看到的却是一种被精神充满的东西，因为耶稣和他的朋友们的观点的性质，不可能与那种把一切都当作机器、工具、器具的观点更加对立，它反倒是对于精神的最高信仰；而凡是人们看到一种行动的凑合的统一的地方——这些行动单个自为地看就缺少这种统一，缺少整个结果的意图——并且把这些行动（比如该亚法的行动）看作服从于它、被它无意识地在与统一的关系中支配和引导的现实性和工具的地方，约翰就看到精神的统一，并且在这种行动本身中看到整个结果的精神在行动；他谈该亚法时，说他自己就被那种精神所充满，而耶稣命运中的必然性就在这种精神里。

en: Thus, too, seen with the soul of the apostles, the miracles lose something of the harshness which the opposition of spirit and body in them has for us, since it is evident that those men lacked the European understanding, which so strips all spirit from what enters consciousness and fixes it into absolute objectivities, into actualities absolutely opposed to spirit, that their cognition is rather an indeterminate hovering between actuality and spirit, which indeed still separated the two, but did not separate them so irrevocably, and moreover did not merge into pure nature, but already gave the clear opposition itself, which with further development had to become a pairing of the living and the dead, of the divine and the actual, which through the placing of the actual Jesus alongside the transfigured, the one become God, showed satisfaction to the deepest drive toward religion, but did not grant it, and made it into an infinite, inextinguishable and unappeased longing; for to the longing, in its highest enthusiasm, in the raptures of the most finely organized souls breathing the highest love, there always stands opposed the individual, something objective, personal, after union with which all the depths of their beautiful feelings languished, but which union, because it is an individual, is eternally impossible, since it always remains over against them, eternally in their consciousness, and never lets religion become complete life.
zh: 所以，用使徒的灵魂来看，奇迹也失去了精神和身体的对立在我们这里所具有的那种生硬，因为可以看到，他们缺少欧洲式的知性，这种知性把一切精神都从进入意识的东西里抽走，把它固定为绝对的客观性、固定为与精神绝对对立的现实性；他们的认识倒毋宁是一种在现实性和精神之间不确定的飘浮，这种飘浮虽然还把两者分开，却没有把它们分得那么不可挽回，而且终究没有合为纯粹的自然，反倒是已经给出了那种清晰的对立，这种对立在进一步发展时必然会变成活的东西与死的东西、神性的东西与现实的东西的配对，而这个配对通过把现实的耶稣与得了荣耀的、变成了神的耶稣并列在一起，向最深的宗教冲动显示出了满足，却没有给予满足，反而把它变成了无限的、不可磨灭的、无法平息的热望；因为对于这种热望来说，在它最高的狂热中、在最精细地组织起来的、呼吸着最高爱的灵魂的沉醉中，总是有那个个体，一个客观的、人格性的东西与它相对而立，而他们美好感受的一切深处都在渴望着与这个个体的结合，但这种结合，因为它是一个个体，永远是不可能的，因为它始终在他们对面，永远留在他们的意识里，使宗教永远不能成为完整的生命。

en: In all forms of the Christian religion that have developed in the continuing fate of time, this fundamental character of opposition rests in the divine, which is supposed to be present only in consciousness, never in life — from the rapturous unions of the enthusiast, who renounces all manifoldness of life, even the purest, in which the spirit enjoys itself, and is conscious only of God, and thus could remove the opposition of personality only in death, up to the actuality of the most manifold consciousness, of the union with the fate of the world and of God's opposition to it — either the felt opposition in all actions and expressions of life, which purchase their legitimacy through the feeling of the servitude and nullity of their opposition, as in the Catholic church, or God's opposition in mere more or less devout thoughts, as in the Protestant church — either the opposition of a hating God to life, as a disgrace and a crime, in some sects of the same, or of a benevolent [God] to life and its joys, as altogether something received, benefits and gifts from him, as altogether actuality, into which then also the form of spirit hovering above it is drawn down, in the idea of a divine man, of the prophets, etc., to historical objective view —: between these extremes of the manifold or diminished consciousness of friendship, of hatred, or of indifference toward the world, between these extremes which lie within the opposition of God and the world, of the divine and of life, the Christian church has run the circle forwards and backwards, but it is against its essential character to find rest in an impersonal living beauty; and it is its fate that church and state, divine service and life, piety and virtue, spiritual and worldly doing can never melt together into one.
zh: 在基督教宗教的一切形式里——这些形式是在时间不断前行的命运中发展出来的——对立的这一基本特征都栖息于神性者之中，而这个神性者应当只在意识里、从不在生命里在场，——从狂热者的那些令人沉醉的结合，即他弃绝生命的一切杂多、也包括最纯粹的杂多（在那种杂多里精神享受自身），并且只意识到上帝，因而只有在死亡中才能去掉人格性的对立，一直到最杂多的意识的现实性、与世界命运的结合以及上帝对世界命运的对立，——要么是在一切行动和生命表现中感受到的那种对立，这类行动和生命表现以自己的对立所带有的奴役性和虚无性的感受来换取自己的合法性，如同在天主教会里那样，要么是在仅仅或多或少虔诚的思想中上帝的对立，如同在新教教会里那样，——要么是某些教派中一个仇恨生命的上帝与生命相对立，把它当作耻辱和罪行，要么是一个仁慈的上帝与生命及其欢乐相对立，把这一切都当作接受来的东西、当作他的恩惠和礼物，当作纯粹的现实性，于是连那悬浮在它之上的精神形式，也在一个神性的人、先知等等的理念中被拉低为历史的客观观点——：在这些极端之间，即在对世界的友谊、仇恨或漠不关心的杂多的或减少了的意识之间，在这些处于上帝与世界、神性者与生命的对立之内的极端之间，基督教会向前和向后跑完了这个圆圈，但要在一种非人格的、活生生的美中找到安宁，却是违背它的本质特征的；而它的命运就是：教会与国家、礼拜与生命、虔诚与美德、宗教的作为与世俗的作为，永远不能融而为一。
